name: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)
title: CWE-918: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)
ai_text: In AI software, CWE-918 shows up mostly in the connectors that let models and agents reach outside tools. The CVEs sit in MCP servers such as MCP Atlassian, mcp-remote and ToolHive, in agent and workflow platforms like Langflow and Flowise, and in model gateways such as LiteLLM and Ollama. The usual route is a URL or hostname supplied through a tool call, a document loader or an OpenAPI import, which the server then fetches without checking where it points. That lets an attacker reach internal services and cloud metadata, or leak tokens such as a GitLab or Azure bearer token, to a host of their choosing.
description: The web server receives a URL or similar request from an upstream component and retrieves the contents of this URL, but it does not sufficiently ensure that the request is being sent to the expected destination.

consequences.note: By providing URLs to unexpected hosts or ports, attackers can make it appear that the server is sending the request, possibly bypassing access controls such as firewalls that prevent the attackers from accessing the URLs directly. The server can be used as a proxy to conduct port scanning of hosts in internal networks, use other URLs such as that can access documents on the system (using file://), or use other protocols such as gopher:// or tftp://, which may provide greater control over the contents of requests.
